background.fact: WPG means WordPerfect Graphic and belongs to the WordPerfect graphics family.
A WPG drawing can combine vector objects with bitmap content.
Corel documents a palette containing as many as 256 selected colors.
Corel distinguishes WPG version 1.0 from version 2.0.
WordPerfect 5.1 and earlier use the version 1.0 export option.
The version 2.0 option targets WordPerfect 6 and newer.

windows.note: Lists WPG among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.
Imports WPG drawings through File > Import; inspect the documented limitations.
Opens WPG as an image or imports it into an existing image.

mac.note: Lists WPG among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

linux.note: Lists WPG among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

problems.fact: Choosing WPG 2.0 is inappropriate when the destination needs WordPerfect 5.1 compatibility.
CorelDRAW documents an import limitation for Graphics Text Type 2.
The documented CorelDRAW importer retains embedded WMF and EMF graphics but can discard other embedded graphic elements.

background.fact: XBM stores an image as readable C source rather than a conventional binary picture.
Its historical uses include icons and pointer artwork for the X graphical environment.
The image representation is monochrome, using black and white.
An XBM export may include coordinates for a pointer hotspot.
GIMP can write an accompanying mask file for an alpha channel.
The older X10 export variant writes short integers instead of individual bytes.

windows.note: Lists XBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

mac.note: Lists XBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

linux.note: Lists XBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

problems.fact: Color artwork becomes monochrome when exported as XBM.
C source representation can consume more space than a binary image encoding.
An added XBM comment can confuse some image viewers.
GIMP requires an 8-bit-per-channel image before its XBM export is available.
A separately exported alpha mask must accompany the bitmap when the receiving workflow uses it.

background.fact: PBM expands to Portable Bit Map and represents two-tone raster images.
Netpbm uses PBM as an intermediate representation between image-processing programs.
A raw PBM image begins with P4 and stores its pixels as packed bits.
P1 identifies the plain variant, whose pixels are readable zeros and ones.
A one bit denotes black; a zero denotes white.
Raw PBM permits consecutive images, while plain PBM contains one image.
The conventional PBM MIME label is image/x-portable-bitmap; Netpbm notes that it is not registered with IANA.

windows.note: Lists PBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

mac.note: Lists PBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

linux.note: Lists PBM among readable image formats; private and educational use is free.

problems.fact: Color and gray shading cannot be represented directly in a two-tone PBM image.
Plain PBM consumes more space because each pixel uses a text digit.
Some readers implement only a restricted subset of the PBM specification.
A reader expecting one image may not handle a raw PBM sequence; Netpbm recommends a minimal single-image layout for interoperability.

background.fact: Apple documents .m4b as an AAC audiobook extension.
Apple lists audio/x-m4b for this audiobook file type in its archived iOS media documentation.
FFmpeg recognizes .m4b through its MOV and MPEG-4 container reader.
The MOV/MPEG-4 family supports chapter metadata, which readers handle separately from audio samples.
M4B is used for audiobooks distributed without DRM as well as in Apple-oriented listening workflows.

windows.note: Reads an unencrypted M4B through its MOV/MPEG-4 demuxer.
Plays media through FFmpeg libraries; support depends on the included demuxers and decoders.

mac.note: Processes unencrypted M4B audio using its MPEG-4 reader.
Uses FFmpeg libraries to play compatible unprotected audio.

linux.note: Accepts M4B input through the MOV/MPEG-4 reader.
FFmpeg-based playback for an accessible audio stream.

mobile.note: iPhone audiobook player with M4B import and chapter navigation; intended for DRM-free audiobooks.

problems.fact: BookPlayer is designed for DRM-free audiobooks, so protected purchases fall outside its stated scope.
Chapter navigation may be missing in a non-seekable FFmpeg input because its MOV reader parses chapters only for seekable input.
Nero-style chapter markers can conflict with some tagging applications; FFmpeg documents an option that writes only a QuickTime chapter track.

background.fact: XML is a markup syntax developed within the World Wide Web Consortium.
Its syntax derives from a subset of SGML.
An XML document contains a single document element with properly nested content.
Elements, attributes, character data, and entities make up its document structure.
Conforming XML processors must accept both UTF-8 and UTF-16.
The fifth edition of XML 1.0 became a W3C Recommendation in November 2008.
RFC 7303 defines application/xml and treats text/xml as its alias.

windows.note: Opens XML source in its XML language mode.
Reads XML and reports parsing errors; available with libxml2.

mac.note: Opens XML source in its XML language mode.
Reads XML and reports parsing errors; available with libxml2.

linux.note: Opens XML source in its XML language mode.
Reads XML and reports parsing errors; available with libxml2.

problems.fact: Unmatched tags or overlapping elements violate XML well-formedness and cause parsing errors.
An undeclared entity reference can make an XML document fail well-formedness checks.
Bytes that disagree with the declared character encoding can make a document unreadable to a conforming parser.
Well-formed syntax does not establish that the data satisfies a particular DTD or application schema.

background.fact: Apple identifies .m4p with protected AAC audio in its archived media-format documentation.
The documented media type for that protected audio is audio/x-m4p.
Older Apple music purchases can use Protected AAC rather than a freely convertible encoding.
Apple applies a five-computer authorization limit to purchases linked to an Apple Account.
Apple also used .m4p in an example preview URL in its iTunes Search API reference.

windows.note: Authorizes a Windows computer for Apple Account purchases; protected tracks require the appropriate account.
NCH documents iTunes playback for protected M4P after account authorization.

mac.note: Plays authorized purchases; Apple documents the authorization workflow on Mac.
NCH documents authorized iTunes playback for M4P; this is a legacy Mac workflow.

problems.fact: Apple Music cannot convert older purchases that remain in Protected AAC format.
A new computer cannot be authorized while all five account authorization slots are occupied.
Authorization must be performed on the computer being authorized, rather than from another device.

background.fact: Mozilla introduced APNG as an animated extension of PNG.
An APNG can use either the .apng or .png filename ending.
The animation uses lossless raster compression.
Animated PNG supports full-color images and optional alpha transparency.
Animation control and frame control chunks describe repetition, frame timing, and composition.
The PNG third edition, published as a W3C Recommendation in June 2025, includes animation.
The PNG specification defines image/apng as an Internet media type.

windows.note: Supports animated PNG playback; Mozilla lists support from Firefox 3.
Supports APNG among its animated image formats.

mac.note: Supports animated PNG playback; Mozilla lists support from Firefox 3.
Supports APNG among its animated image formats.

linux.note: Supports animated PNG playback; Mozilla lists support from Firefox 3.
Supports APNG among its animated image formats.

web.note: Displays APNG without the extension suggested by the wiki; support is listed from Chrome 59.

mobile.note: Mozilla lists Safari support from version 8; browser playback includes APNG.

Android browser for viewing APNG images within web pages; Mozilla documents Firefox APNG playback and its Gecko-based Android implementation. This entry does not promise image editing or system gallery integration.

problems.fact: A decoder that does not process animation can show the default PNG image instead.
The default image is not required to belong to the animation, so a still preview may differ from its first animated frame.
Incorrect frame sequence numbers signal an invalid animated PNG stream.
Incorrect blend or disposal handling can leave remnants of earlier frames in an animation.

background.fact: ALAC is Apple's lossless audio codec, rather than a standalone image or video format.
Apple's reference implementation supports 16-, 20-, 24-, and 32-bit sample depths.
The reference codec accepts configurations ranging from one to eight audio channels.
Apple documents integer sample rates through 384,000 Hz for its implementation.
Its default packet contains 4,096 sample frames.
Apple distributes source for both encoding and decoding ALAC.
Apple Music offers lossless listening using Apple Lossless audio technology.

windows.note: Apple's sample utility reads ALAC in CAF; a Windows project is provided.
Offers Apple Lossless encoding and playback of imported songs.

mac.note: Apple's example converter accepts ALAC CAF input; its Xcode project targets Mac OS X.
Supports the service's lossless playback; playback hardware and sample-rate limits still apply.

linux.note: Includes an ALAC decoder; the enclosing container must also be readable.
Apple provides a UNIX/Linux makefile; the sample utility handles ALAC CAF.

problems.fact: The sample alacconvert utility implements fewer channel and file-layout combinations than the underlying codec.
Nondefault ALAC packet sizes are not guaranteed to work on every supporting hardware device.
Apple Music lossless downloads consume more device storage than its compressed alternatives.
Some Mac playback setups need an external DAC for sample rates above 48 kHz.
